http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/29/kazak.text: Kazakhstan has entered a new political season with a reshaped political system after the country’s newly established unicameral parliament, with its lawmakers gathered for its first session on Friday in Astana.It comes Kazakhstan’s pro-government Adilet party won more than 71 percent of the vote in last Sunday’s parliamentary election, that was triggered by a new constitution adopted earlier this year.The session attended by all 145 members opened with an address by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, who formally declared the first session of the first convocation of the Kurultai open and described it as the beginning of an important new stage in the country’s development.“From this day, the process of renewing the country’s political system begins. … The Kurultai will fundamentally modernise the system of government and give a powerful impetus to the work of the entire state apparatus.By improving the quality of national legislation, the Kurultai will provide a strong foundation for the country’s legal system,” Tokayev said.A new political systemUnder the Constitution, the government is required to step down before a newly elected Kurultai. Kazakhstan’s government therefore relinquished its powers as the new parliament convened.However, the country will not be left without a functioning government during the transition period. President Tokayev signed a decree instructing the cabinet to continue performing its duties until a new government is formed.Under Kazakhstan’s new Constitution, which came into force on 1 July 2026, the previous bicameral parliament, consisting of the Mazhilis and the Senate, was replaced by a unicameral parliament called the Kurultai.The term “kurultai” dates back centuries and historically referred to an assembly or council among the peoples of the Great Steppe.The new Constitution was adopted in a nationwide referendum held on 15 March 2026.“By coming together, our people accomplished a great deal in a very short period of time. Thanks to the nationwide referendum, the country successfully implemented a sweeping constitutional reform,” Tokayev said.The Kurultai consists of 145 lawmakers elected for five-year terms and representing five political parties. The Adilet party, which absorbed Amanat, the successor to the long-dominant Nur Otan party, holds a commanding majority with 110 seats.It is followed by the Auyl party with 10 seats, Respublica with nine, the Nationwide Social Democratic Party (OSDP) with eight and Ak Zhol with eight.New speaker of the KurultaiDuring the session, President Tokayev nominated Aibek Dadebai for the position of chairman of the Kurultai. Dadebai has headed the Adilet party since 7 May 2026 and has held several senior government and diplomatic posts, including serving as head of the Presidential Administration from February 2024 to May 2026.Tokayev said Dadebai had extensive experience in public administration and described him as an educated, patriotic and responsible citizen. “I consider him worthy of this position and ask the members of the Kurultai to support his candidacy,” Tokayev said.Later in the day, lawmakers backed the nomination and elected Dadebai chairman of the Kurultai in a secret ballot.Lawmakers also elected three deputy speakers: former senator Nurlan Beknazarov, former Mazhilis deputy speaker Dania Espaeva and Children’s Rights Commissioner Dinara Zakiyeva.The Kurultai will have eight standing committees, seven of which will be chaired by representatives of the ruling Adilet party, while the remaining committee will be headed by a member of the Auyl party.What happens next?Kazakhstan’s new political structure will continue to take shape in the coming weeks. Once the Kurultai is fully organised, President Tokayev will put forward candidates for vice-president and prime minister, before appointing the new government following consultations with lawmakers. A deputy chairman of the Security Council will also be appointed to a newly created post.Tokayev said he would deliver his annual address to the nation once the new parliament and government are fully formed.The institutional changes will continue into September, with the Kazakhstan People’s Council expected to be established in the second half of the month. The new constitutional body will represent the country’s ethnic, regional, social and political diversity and will have the right to initiate legislation.According to Tokayev, the process will renew “almost all key institutions of power” within a relatively short period.

Martinez/Austin American-Statesman/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement A man has been hospitalized in Austin, Texas after being shot by an officer of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) , local officials said Sunday. Austin's Mayor Kirk Watson expressed his anger over the shooting, calling for the involvement of the local police in a "clear-eyed" investigation into the incident. What do we know about the ICE shooting in Austin? The man suffered one gunshot wound in his torso during a brief foot pursuit in the Texan capital's north side shortly before 1 pm local time, Austin officials said at a press briefing. He is at a local hospital in a serious but stable condition, the officials said, adding that the information on the incident was "very preliminary." City police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said. Who is the man wounded by ICE agent? The officials did not name the man or release his age and nationality but an immigration lawyer, representing his family, identified him as Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan. Attorney Kate Lincoln Goldfinch said in a video published on her Instagram account that she believed he had no criminal history and had no final order to be removed from the country. The Associated Press later cited Goldfinch as saying that she did not know his current immigration status. There is yet to be a statement on the shooting from ICE or the Department of Homeland Security that oversees the immigration agency. Meanwhile, a group of about 100 protesters gathered at the site of the shooting and demonstrated against ICE's actions. Demonstrators protest at the scene of the shooting Image: Kaylee Greenlee/REUTERS The protest was held across the street from a blue Toyota Corolla which had damage to its ​passenger-side door, news agency Reuters reported citing local TV, as ICE agents stood nearby. The damaged car was towed away Image: Jesse Bedayn/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Austin Mayor rails against 'rogue' ICE, calls for independent probe Sunday's shooting is the latest in a slew of incidents involving ICE, which has become the face of an immigration clampdown by US President Donald Trump's Republican administration. Watson, a Democrat, told the media that the shooting occurred amid a "significant increase, almost overnight" of ICE operations in Austin. "While I'm angry and disappointed, I'm not surprised. This has happened in other cities. With the rogue nature of ICE and the chaos we're seeing fomented by ICE, there's no reason to be surprised," the Austin mayor wrote on X. He called for an independent investigation into the shooting, with the Austin Police Department (APD) having a role in the probe. He said that the people of Austin had a "right to know what happened" and "a right to feel safe in their community". "Though APD was not involved in the shooting, I believe that there needs to be an investigation that APD assures is clear-eyed, as complete as possible, and independent," Watson said. He added that police chief Davis had deployed the APD's Special Investigation Unit at the scene, elaborating that the unit is the one responsible for probing Austin's officer-involved shootings. Watson said that Davis has also asked the Texas Rangers to help out in the investigation. 'Horror has come to our doorstep,' says Congressman On Sunday, US Representative Greg Casar — a Texas Democrat — called for transparency as the shooting is investigated. He accused ICE of not being "truthful" in shooting in other cities . "It is awful that this horror has come to our doorstep," Casar said. "A few weeks ago as we saw the ICE surge come ... I and others said that ICE needed to leave before someone was shot," he told the media. Illustration: Rocco Fazzari/AAP View image in fullscreen Beau Lamarre-Condon has made his first statement to the court, after pleading not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies. Illustration: Rocco Fazzari/AAP New South Wales Beau Lamarre-Condon tells jury he wanted to report deaths but friend encouraged him to dispose of bodies NSW police officer accused of murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies tells court he wanted to do ‘right thing’ by their families Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Jordyn Beazley Mon 26 Oct 2026 22.18 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 22.51 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Beau Lamarre-Condon has accused a friend of encouraging him to dispose of the bodies of two men “straight away” despite him wanting to report the deaths to police, according to his first statement to his double murder trial. Lamarre-Condon, 31, is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter. His legal team has argued that Baird and Davies were accidentally shot, and that he had acted in “self-defence”. One of his friends, known to the court under the pseudonym Elizabeth Kennedy, had accompanied Lamarre-Condon while he allegedly disposed of the bodies, the trial has heard. She gave evidence last week that she thought she and the then-police officer were going out for lunch when he picked her up, two days after the alleged murders. She denied in court helping Lamarre-Condon and said “I didn’t know anything”. Covert recording of prison meeting between Beau Lamarre-Condon and friend played to double murder trial Read more On Tuesday, Lamarre-Condon had a statement read to court that contradicted Kennedy’s version of events. He alleged in the statement that Kennedy “flat-out lied to police in her statement regarding her involvement” and he wanted to do the “right thing” by the families of Baird and Davies because “they deserve to know the truth, too”. In the statement read to the court by prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC, Lamarre-Condon alleged that after he picked up Kennedy, he showed her the bodies in the back of a van. He alleged that he began to cry and then said to Kennedy: “I should just drive straight to the police now, shouldn’t I?” Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Lamarre-Condon told the court that Kennedy replied: “No, no, you can’t. They won’t believe you. “This is like Taylor Swift’s song, No Body, No Crime. We have to get rid of them straight away,” she allegedly said. According to his statement, Lamarre-Condon warned Kennedy she could be charged as an accessory to murder, and he would not be mad if she walked away “right now”. He alleged that she said she would help him because he “would help me if I ever needed … help with anything”. He also told the court that while they drove, Kennedy played the song “No Body, No Crime” by Taylor Swift on her phone and “began laughing at the situation”. He alleged Kennedy then assisted with carrying the bodies and helped pour concrete into the bags to help them sink after they arrived at a farm in Bungonia. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “When the bag [wouldn’t] sink, [Kennedy] got my pocketknife out … and tried to cut multiple holes into the surfboard cover. This is where Luke got the knife wounds in his leg,” Lamarre-Condon said in his statement. “Whilst [Kennedy] was assisting me on the farm, at no point did she say she didn’t want to assist or have any part in it. She was a willing participant.” He said he initially didn’t tell police about Kennedy’s involvement in disposing of the bodies because she had begged him not to. He alleged he told her that if it went before court, he’d have to tell the truth because he “can’t lie under oath”. Last week, Kennedy told the court she did not willingly help Lamarre-Condon, nor did she help to sink the bodies. While under questioning by Lamarre-Condon’s barrister, John Stratton SC, she said: “I didn’t know anything. I’m five foot and weigh 55 kilos so I don’t think I could carry a body even if I tried.” Kennedy told the court that she waited at a gate while Lamarre-Condon drove out of sight to a dam on the farm. She denied that Lamarre-Condon had told her Baird was dead. She also alleged it was him who played the Swift song in the car. “He was the one that put that song on in the car … it’s a very niche song,” she told the court last week. The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.
